title: ACID: a money transfer that cannot go wrong
intro: Move 100 from Alice to Bob. That is two updates. What if the app dies between them?

predict.question: The app crashes after taking 100 from Alice but before giving it to Bob. What is Alice's balance after recovery?
predict.reveal: Atomicity: the transaction is all or nothing. The half-done debit is rolled back, so Alice is back at 500.

takeaway: ACID: Atomic (all or nothing), Consistent (rules hold), Isolated (no peeking mid-way), Durable (committed stays saved).

steps.say: Alice has 500 and Bob has 200, 700 in total. We want to move 100 from Alice to Bob safely.
The app opens a transaction. Think of it as a bubble: everything inside happens together or not at all.
First update: take 100 from Alice. Right now the money has left Alice but not yet reached Bob.
Disaster: the app crashes before it can credit Bob. 100 has gone missing from the books.
Atomicity: the database sees the transaction never committed and undoes it. Alice is back to 500.
The app restarts and retries, this time sending both updates inside one transaction.
Consistency: the database checks its rules. Balances are not negative and the total is still 700. The rules hold.
Isolation: until this transaction commits, other sessions still see A=500 and B=200. Nobody sees the money half-moved.
The app says COMMIT. This is the point of no return, where the changes become official.
Durability: before answering, the database writes the change to the log on disk.
Only now does the database confirm to the app. The transfer is complete.
Even if the power dies right now, on restart the database replays the disk log and shows A=400 B=300.
